title: Flat-Band Stoner Instability and Peierls-Phase Origin of the Transdimensional Anomalous Hall Effect in Rhombohedral Graphite
abstract: A ``transdimensional'' anomalous Hall effect (TDAHE), where both in-plane ($\Bpar$) and out-of-plane magnetic fields produce hysteretic Hall signals, was recently observed in nine-layer rhombohedral graphite~\cite{Li2026Nature}. We present a microscopic theory attributing the TDAHE to a flat-band Stoner instability coupled to Peierls-phase gap modulation. The flat-band density of states satisfies the Stoner criterion $Uρ(\varepsilon_F) > 1$~\cite{Bultinck2020}, driving a spin-valley-locked ferromagnet whose valley polarization $η$ breaks time-reversal symmetry and generates an intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC). The orbital $g$-factor $g_{\mathrm{orb}} = e d_0 v_F (N{-}1)/2 \propto (N{-}1)$ then lets $\Bpar$ modulate the gap, producing the transdimensional response $\propto η$. A self-consistent $2N$-band Hartree-Fock calculation yields complete valley polarization ($η\to 1$) below a mean-field transition $T_c^{\mathrm{MF}} \approx 2.2$~K, reduced by 2D-Ising critical fluctuations to the experimental $T_c \approx 1.6$~K, with $R_{xy} \approx 1.5$~k$Ω$. Because both Hall responses are carried by one order parameter $η$, they share a single $T_c$, as observed; $T_c$ is governed by the Stoner product $Uρ$ and is insensitive to the intervalley exchange, which only gates whether the valley-polarized phase forms, so the exchange strength is not a fitted parameter. Beyond reproducing $R_{xy}$, $T_c$, and the phase window, the theory predicts a sharp onset of valley polarization between $N = 7$ and $N = 9$, a symmetry selection rule fixing the crescent Fermi surface to the $m{=}1$ nematic channel, and a transdimensional-to-conventional Hall ratio $\sigmaPHE/\sigmaAHE^{\mathrm{tot}} = g_{\mathrm{orb}}\Bpar/m$ independent of $η$ and $U$. The $Z$-independence of the intrinsic AHC is verified within dynamical mean-field theory.
summary: This work provides a comprehensive microscopic theory explaining the Transdimensional Anomalous Hall Effect in rhombohedral graphite. It attributes the effect to a Stoner instability that induces spin-valley polarization ($\eta$), which simultaneously controls both the intrinsic and planar components of the anomalous Hall response. The theoretical framework successfully predicts key experimental signatures like the common critical temperature ($T_c$) across different magnetic field orientations.
main_problem: The paper develops a microscopic theory for the Transdimensional Anomalous Hall Effect (TDAHE) observed in rhombohedral graphite.
main_result: The TDAHE is attributed to a flat-band Stoner instability coupled to Peierls-phase gap modulation, leading to a common critical temperature ($T_c$) governing both AHE and TDAHE responses.
method: Theoretical calculations employing self-consistent Hartree-Fock methods, Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT), and comparison with Ising model simulations are used.
model_or_system: The system is nine-layer rhombohedral graphite modeled by an $N$-layer ABC-stacked Hamiltonian. The physics hinges on the Stoner criterion ($Uho(\epsilon_F) > 1$) driving spin-valley polarization ($\eta$).
key_observables: Anomalous Hall Conductivity ($\sigma_{	ext{int}}^{xy}$), Transdimensional AHE component ($\sigma_{	ext{PHE}}^{xy}$), and the common critical temperature ($T_c$).
important_parameters: $N$ (number of layers, $N \ge 5$), Stoner interaction strength ($Uho$), orbital g-factor ($g_{	ext{orb}} \propto N-1$).
main_assumptions: The theory assumes the TDAHE is governed by a single order parameter ($\eta$) and that correlation effects are captured by mean-field treatments, with DMFT confirming $Z$-independence.
figures_summary: Figures compare theoretical predictions of valley polarization $\eta(T)$ against experimental bounds, showing agreement in the 2D Ising critical fluctuation regime for $T_c$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the TDAHE phenomenon to proposing the Stoner instability mechanism. It then derives the mathematical dependence of both Hall responses on the valley polarization $\eta$ and the orbital g-factor, culminating in quantitative predictions for $T_c$ and layer scaling.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of how a magnetic instability (Stoner) couples to structural/orbital effects (Peierls phase) to generate multiple correlated transport responses is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in strongly interacting electronic systems.

The valley order saturates at η →1 and vanishes at T MF c ≈ 2.2 K (blue dashed). Shaded band: localized-Ising Tc bracket [1.34, 2.05] K (NN lower bound, bare-1/r upper bound; inter- mediate ranges give ≈1.9 K, dash-dot, Supplementary). Red dotted: experimental Tc = 1.6 K [1]; grey dotted: SCR lower bound ≳0.9 K.

FIG. 2. Insensitivity of Tc to the intervalley exchange. Self- consistent 2N-band Hartree-Fock T MF c (Viv/U) for N = 9 at D = 0.85 V/nm, at the experimental density n = 1.4 × 1012 cm−2 (orange) and a lower density (blue). Tc saturates at ≈2.2 K for Viv/U ≳0.75; below ∼0.65 the valley polariza- tion is lost. Red dotted: experimental Tc = 1.6 K [1].

FIG. 3. Self-consistent valley polarization η(n) (left axis, red) at D = 0.9 V/nm (N = 9, T = 0.5 K), saturated (η →1) for n ≲1.8 × 1012 cm−2. Right axis: experimental ∆Rxy at B∥= 0 (digitized from Extended Data Fig. 6 of Ref. 1), purple/orange for ∆Rxy ≶0. η is the order-parameter mag- nitude, so it stays saturated across the switching window (n = 1.6–1.9) while the ∆Rxy sign reverses at n ≈1.83, marking the valley flavour switch K ↔K′ at fixed |η|. Yellow band: switching window; dotted lines mark hysteresis onset (n = 1.0) and loop collapse (n = 2.0, into the quarter-metal phase).
